--- title: "SQL Questions" --- All queries run on the schema FAA, which has the fact table al_perf and the lookup tables. For the delay questions (1, 2, 4 and 5) I only use flights that have a departure time, because mysqlimport saved the empty delays of cancelled flights as 0. ## Problem 1 *Find maximal departure delay in minutes for each airline. Sort results from smallest to largest maximum delay. Output airline names and values of the delay.* ```sql SELECT a.Name AS airline_name, MAX(p.DepDelay) AS max_departure_delay_minutes FROM al_perf p JOIN L_AIRLINE_ID a ON a.ID = p.DOT_ID_Reporting_Airline WHERE p.DepTime <> '' GROUP BY a.ID, a.Name ORDER BY max_departure_delay_minutes ASC; ``` ::: {#5f7cbe24 .cell execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=2} | airline_name | max_departure_delay_minutes | |:---------------------------|------------------------------:| | Southwest Airlines Co.: WN | 610 | | Alaska Airlines Inc.: AS | 684 | | Delta Air Lines Inc.: DL | 1,174 | | Endeavor Air Inc.: 9E | 1,246 | | Republic Airline: YX | 1,289 | | Frontier Airlines Inc.: F9 | 1,305 | | Spirit Air Lines: NK | 1,396 | | Hawaiian Airlines Inc.: HA | 1,441 | | Allegiant Air: G4 | 1,523 | | Envoy Air: MQ | 1,546 | | SkyWest Airlines Inc.: OO | 1,627 | | United Air Lines Inc.: UA | 1,804 | | JetBlue Airways: B6 | 1,838 | | PSA Airlines Inc.: OH | 2,629 | | American Airlines Inc.: AA | 3,125 | ::: ::: ::: {#fec3c3f6 .cell execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: Southwest had the smallest maximum delay (610 minutes) and American the largest (3,125 minutes, about 52 hours). Every airline had at least one flight that was more than 10 hours late. [Download CSV](data/hw4_cheng_zhiyang_zc385_problem1.csv) ## Problem 2 *Find maximal early departures in minutes for each airline. Sort results from largest to smallest. Output airline names.* An early departure has a negative DepDelay, so the earliest one is `-MIN(DepDelay)`. ```sql SELECT a.Name AS airline_name, -MIN(p.DepDelay) AS max_early_departure_minutes FROM al_perf p JOIN L_AIRLINE_ID a ON a.ID = p.DOT_ID_Reporting_Airline WHERE p.DepTime <> '' AND p.DepDelay < 0 GROUP BY a.ID, a.Name ORDER BY max_early_departure_minutes DESC; ``` ::: {#d680edc4 .cell execution_count=4} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=4} | airline_name | max_early_departure_minutes | |:---------------------------|------------------------------:| | Alaska Airlines Inc.: AS | 56 | | Allegiant Air: G4 | 44 | | SkyWest Airlines Inc.: OO | 43 | | United Air Lines Inc.: UA | 37 | | Delta Air Lines Inc.: DL | 36 | | Frontier Airlines Inc.: F9 | 35 | | JetBlue Airways: B6 | 34 | | Republic Airline: YX | 34 | | Endeavor Air Inc.: 9E | 32 | | PSA Airlines Inc.: OH | 32 | | Spirit Air Lines: NK | 27 | | Envoy Air: MQ | 24 | | American Airlines Inc.: AA | 23 | | Hawaiian Airlines Inc.: HA | 22 | | Southwest Airlines Co.: WN | 19 | ::: ::: Alaska had the earliest departure, 56 minutes before schedule. Southwest never left more than 19 minutes early. [Download CSV](data/hw4_cheng_zhiyang_zc385_problem2.csv) ## Problem 3 *Rank days of the week by the number of flights performed by all airlines on that day (1 is the busiest). Output the day of the week names, number of flights and ranks in the rank increasing order.* ```sql SELECT w.Day AS day_of_week, COUNT(*) AS num_flights, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS day_rank FROM al_perf p JOIN L_WEEKDAYS w ON w.Code = p.DayOfWeek GROUP BY w.Code, w.Day ORDER BY day_rank; ``` ::: {#11e194b0 .cell execution_count=5} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=5} | day_of_week | num_flights | day_rank | |:--------------|--------------:|-----------:| | Monday | 91,299 | 1 | | Wednesday | 85,719 | 2 | | Tuesday | 85,106 | 3 | | Friday | 74,105 | 4 | | Thursday | 73,913 | 5 | | Sunday | 73,615 | 6 | | Saturday | 63,514 | 7 | ::: ::: ::: {#8eeb1d44 .cell execution_count=6} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: Monday is the busiest day with 91,299 flights and Saturday the quietest. January 2024 had five Mondays, Tuesdays and Wednesdays and only four of the other days, which is a big reason those three days are at the top. [Download CSV](data/hw4_cheng_zhiyang_zc385_problem3.csv) ## Problem 4 *Find the airport that has the highest average departure delay among all airports. Consider 0 minutes delay for flights that departed early. Output one line of results: the airport name, code, and average delay.* `GREATEST(DepDelay, 0)` counts early departures as 0 minutes. ```sql SELECT ap.Name AS airport_name, p.Origin AS airport_code, ROUND(AVG(GREATEST(p.DepDelay, 0)), 2) AS avg_departure_delay_minutes FROM al_perf p JOIN L_AIRPORT ap ON ap.Code = p.Origin WHERE p.DepTime <> '' GROUP BY p.Origin, ap.Name ORDER BY AVG(GREATEST(p.DepDelay, 0)) DESC LIMIT 1; ``` ::: {#2f7fd173 .cell execution_count=7} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=7} | airport_name | airport_code | avg_departure_delay_minutes | |:-----------------------------------------------------|:---------------|------------------------------:| | Clarksburg/Fairmont, WV: North Central West Virginia | CKB | 86.00 | ::: ::: North Central West Virginia airport (CKB) had the highest average delay, 86 minutes. It only had 15 departures in January. [Download CSV](data/hw4_cheng_zhiyang_zc385_problem4.csv) ## Problem 5 *For each airline find an airport where it has the highest average departure delay. Output an airline name, a name of the airport that has the highest average delay, and the value of that average delay.* The CTE gets each airline's average delay at each airport, and `RANK()` keeps the top airport for each airline. ```sql WITH airline_airport AS ( SELECT p.DOT_ID_Reporting_Airline AS airline_id, p.Origin AS airport_code, AVG(GREATEST(p.DepDelay, 0)) AS avg_delay FROM al_perf p WHERE p.DepTime <> '' GROUP BY p.DOT_ID_Reporting_Airline, p.Origin ), ranked AS ( SELECT airline_id, airport_code, avg_delay, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY airline_id ORDER BY avg_delay DESC) AS rnk FROM airline_airport ) SELECT a.Name AS airline_name, ap.Name AS airport_name, ROUND(r.avg_delay, 2) AS avg_departure_delay_minutes FROM ranked r JOIN L_AIRLINE_ID a ON a.ID = r.airline_id JOIN L_AIRPORT ap ON ap.Code = r.airport_code WHERE r.rnk = 1 ORDER BY r.avg_delay DESC; ``` ::: {#18d3d580 .cell execution_count=8} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=8} | airline_name | airport_name | avg_departure_delay_minutes | |:---------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------:| | PSA Airlines Inc.: OH | Syracuse, NY: Syracuse Hancock International | 217.00 | | Allegiant Air: G4 | New Orleans, LA: Louis Armstrong New Orleans International | 139.75 | | SkyWest Airlines Inc.: OO | Philadelphia, PA: Philadelphia International | 128.82 | | JetBlue Airways: B6 | Minneapolis, MN: Minneapolis-St Paul International | 126.93 | | American Airlines Inc.: AA | Portland, ME: Portland International Jetport | 121.60 | | Envoy Air: MQ | Waco, TX: Waco Regional | 111.87 | | Delta Air Lines Inc.: DL | Cedar Rapids/Iowa City, IA: The Eastern Iowa | 111.40 | | Hawaiian Airlines Inc.: HA | Boston, MA: Logan International | 99.33 | | United Air Lines Inc.: UA | Bend/Redmond, OR: Roberts Field | 78.24 | | Spirit Air Lines: NK | Lafayette, LA: Lafayette Regional Paul Fournet Field | 73.00 | | Endeavor Air Inc.: 9E | Milwaukee, WI: General Mitchell International | 69.41 | | Alaska Airlines Inc.: AS | Lihue, HI: Lihue Airport | 64.74 | | Frontier Airlines Inc.: F9 | Hartford, CT: Bradley International | 60.22 | | Republic Airline: YX | Sarasota/Bradenton, FL: Sarasota/Bradenton International | 55.40 | | Southwest Airlines Co.: WN | Des Moines, IA: Des Moines International | 24.53 | ::: ::: PSA at Syracuse has the highest value, 217 minutes. Many of these averages come from very few flights. For example, Spirit's worst airport (Lafayette, LA) had only one Spirit departure. [Download CSV](data/hw4_cheng_zhiyang_zc385_problem5.csv) ## Problem 6a *Check if your dataset has any canceled flights.* ```sql SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_flights, SUM(Cancelled = 1) AS cancelled_flights, ROUND(100 * SUM(Cancelled = 1) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_cancelled FROM al_perf; ``` ::: {#06daa7ed .cell execution_count=9} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=9} | total_flights | cancelled_flights | pct_cancelled | |----------------:|--------------------:|----------------:| | 547,271.00 | 20,389.00 | 3.73 | ::: ::: Yes. 20,389 of the 547,271 flights (3.73%) were cancelled. [Download CSV](data/hw4_cheng_zhiyang_zc385_problem6a.csv) ## Problem 6b *If it does, what was the most frequent reason for each departure airport? Output airport name, the most frequent reason, and the number of cancelations for that reason.* ```sql WITH airport_reason AS ( SELECT p.Origin AS airport_code, p.CancellationCode, COUNT(*) AS num_cancellations FROM al_perf p WHERE p.Cancelled = 1 GROUP BY p.Origin, p.CancellationCode ), ranked AS ( SELECT airport_code, CancellationCode, num_cancellations, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY airport_code ORDER BY num_cancellations DESC) AS rnk FROM airport_reason ) SELECT ap.Name AS airport_name, c.Reason AS most_frequent_reason, r.num_cancellations FROM ranked r JOIN L_AIRPORT ap ON ap.Code = r.airport_code JOIN L_CANCELATION c ON c.Code = r.CancellationCode WHERE r.rnk = 1 ORDER BY r.num_cancellations DESC, airport_name, most_frequent_reason; ``` The first 15 of 301 rows: ::: {#75bef270 .cell execution_count=10} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=10} | airport_name | most_frequent_reason | num_cancellations | |:-------------------------------------------------------|:-----------------------|--------------------:| | Chicago, IL: Chicago O'Hare International | Weather | 946 | | Seattle, WA: Seattle/Tacoma International | Carrier | 870 | | Dallas/Fort Worth, TX: Dallas/Fort Worth International | Weather | 596 | | Washington, DC: Ronald Reagan Washington National | Weather | 594 | | Newark, NJ: Newark Liberty International | Carrier | 555 | | San Francisco, CA: San Francisco International | Carrier | 516 | | Denver, CO: Denver International | Weather | 492 | | Chicago, IL: Chicago Midway International | Weather | 484 | | New York, NY: LaGuardia | Weather | 474 | | Nashville, TN: Nashville International | Weather | 443 | | Los Angeles, CA: Los Angeles International | Carrier | 370 | | Houston, TX: George Bush Intercontinental/Houston | Carrier | 335 | | San Diego, CA: San Diego International | Carrier | 307 | | Detroit, MI: Detroit Metro Wayne County | Weather | 299 | | Charlotte, NC: Charlotte Douglas International | Weather | 259 | ::: ::: 296 airports had at least one cancellation. At 5 of them two reasons tie for first, so the result has 301 rows. Weather was the top reason at 253 airports. Carrier was the top reason at 45, including Seattle, Newark, San Francisco, Los Angeles and Houston, which are Alaska and United hubs. [Download CSV](data/hw4_cheng_zhiyang_zc385_problem6b.csv) ## Problem 7 *Build a report that for each day output average number of flights considering the current and the previous two days.* `ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` gives the 3-day moving average. January 1 and 2 use only the days that exist. ```sql WITH daily AS ( SELECT FlightDate, COUNT(*) AS num_flights FROM al_perf GROUP BY FlightDate ) SELECT FlightDate AS flight_date, num_flights, ROUND(AVG(num_flights) OVER (ORDER BY FlightDate ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS avg_flights_3day FROM daily ORDER BY FlightDate; ``` ::: {#2563ac93 .cell execution_count=11} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {#aaa4eb4e .cell execution_count=12} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=12} | flight_date | num_flights | avg_flights_3day | |:--------------|--------------:|-------------------:| | 2024-01-01 | 17,265 | 17,265.00 | | 2024-01-02 | 18,977 | 18,121.00 | | 2024-01-03 | 18,520 | 18,254.00 | | 2024-01-04 | 18,066 | 18,521.00 | | 2024-01-05 | 18,109 | 18,231.67 | | 2024-01-06 | 16,950 | 17,708.33 | | 2024-01-07 | 18,812 | 17,957.00 | | 2024-01-08 | 18,472 | 18,078.00 | | 2024-01-09 | 16,775 | 18,019.67 | | 2024-01-10 | 16,795 | 17,347.33 | | 2024-01-11 | 18,500 | 17,356.67 | | 2024-01-12 | 18,590 | 17,961.67 | | 2024-01-13 | 15,483 | 17,524.33 | | 2024-01-14 | 17,583 | 17,218.67 | | 2024-01-15 | 18,620 | 17,228.67 | | 2024-01-16 | 16,530 | 17,577.67 | | 2024-01-17 | 16,877 | 17,342.33 | | 2024-01-18 | 18,663 | 17,356.67 | | 2024-01-19 | 18,698 | 18,079.33 | | 2024-01-20 | 15,535 | 17,632.00 | | 2024-01-21 | 18,573 | 17,602.00 | | 2024-01-22 | 18,559 | 17,555.67 | | 2024-01-23 | 16,472 | 17,868.00 | | 2024-01-24 | 16,837 | 17,289.33 | | 2024-01-25 | 18,684 | 17,331.00 | | 2024-01-26 | 18,708 | 18,076.33 | | 2024-01-27 | 15,546 | 17,646.00 | | 2024-01-28 | 18,647 | 17,633.67 | | 2024-01-29 | 18,383 | 17,525.33 | | 2024-01-30 | 16,352 | 17,794.00 | | 2024-01-31 | 16,690 | 17,141.67 | ::: ::: The daily count goes from about 15,500 to 19,000 and drops every Saturday. The 3-day average smooths this out and stays between about 17,100 and 18,500. [Download CSV](data/hw4_cheng_zhiyang_zc385_problem7.csv)
